items.title: Live: US launches another round of strikes against Iran after Trump threatens to attack 'very hard'
items.description: The US military says it has launched a series of strikes on "multiple targets" in Iran. Follow live.

items.title: Albanese's frustration with Trump is becoming harder to hide
items.description: The Albanese government is paying an economic and political toll for an ongoing and deeply unpopular war.

items.title: Live: One Nation fundraising drive receives $1.6m in donations
items.description: One Nation says it has received $1.6 million in donations after launching a drive in response to a Labor fundraising campaign. Follow live.

items.title: Government flags risk of relying on Elon Musk's SpaceX and Starlink
items.description: As tens of thousands of Australians line up to buy shares in Elon Musk's SpaceX blockbuster public offering, Australian government officials are privately flagging the risks posed by the country's growing reliance on its satellite internet service, Starlink.

items.title: What happens when a gas company abandons an entire city?
items.description: For many, getting off gas and electrifying their homes is a personal choice. But what happens when an entire town is abandoned by a gas company?

items.title: Belfast attack victim's family calls for calm after night of violence
items.description: The family of Belfast stabbing victim Stephen Ogilvie releases a statement saying anti-immigrant violence that has seen houses and a bus torched is "not welcome".

items.title: Why the Belfast stabbing could ignite a summer of unrest
items.description: As UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer fights for his political life, the country is bracing for what could be a yet another summer of unrest.

items.title: Live: ASX set to fall after Wall Street closed down
items.description: The Australian market is set to fall after Wall Street closed down. Meanwhile, President Donald Trump says the US military is "going to be attacking" Iran if no peace deal is agreed. Follow live.

items.title: Massive whale graveyard found in deep ocean off Australia
items.description: Hundreds of whale fossils, including those from extinct species new to science, range in age from recent to 5 million years old and are also home to undescribed deep-sea creatures.

items.title: 'People are just killing themselves': Solariums operating underground
items.description: Illegal solariums are operating across the country, from single machines secretly set up in suburban neighbourhood garages to those hidden in the back of legitimate businesses.

items.title: Gout sixth in Diamond League debut as Olympic champ claims victory
items.description: Gout Gout finishes well back in the field in the men's 200 metres at the Oslo Diamond League meet, with Olympic champion Letsile Tebogo first across the line.

items.title: Grandfather's fall inspires 20yo student's smart clock invention
items.description: After it took nearly two days for his grandfather to be found following a serious fall, Kai Gould has created a device to connect older people living independently with their loved ones.

items.title: 'Very unfair': Collapsed petrol empire lands deal to pay fraction of $13m debt
items.description: The directors of Zoya Investments have agreed to a $2 million settlement to end the liquidator's case against them.

items.title: Predictive text in 'demonstrable decline' with AI-based language models
items.description: If internet chatter is to be believed, the intuitiveness and efficiency of predictive text and autocorrect have fallen off a cliff in recent years. But while researchers agree there has been a demonstrable decline in quality, the increasing sophistication of what phones can do is also making errors more prominent.

items.title: In Moldova, I meet a woman with a dangerous plan to save her life
items.description: On a park bench in Moldova, I meet a Ukrainian refugee who is planning to return home through a war zone for cancer treatment. We talk for hours.

items.title: Spielberg's Disclosure Day is a close encounter of the hopeful kind
items.description: ET director Steven Spielberg dives back into the extra terrestrial with his latest film while asking 'How do you astonish an audience when anything is possible, and nothing is real?

items.title: How well do you know Aussie books? Take our quiz to find out
items.description: Occupy yourself with some armchair travel courtesy of a selection of our nation's most esteemed literary works.

items.title: Pope Leo blesses Barcelona's Sagrada Familia as an 'architectural masterpiece'
items.description: The pontiff has celebrated Spain's Sagrada Familia Basilica as a masterpiece of "stones, colours and light," as he marked the centenary of the death of its architect Antoni Gaudí.

items.title: Bakery trains staff to assess counterfeit notes amid rise in use in SA
items.description: An Adelaide business owner who has been targeted by counterfeiters about a dozen times is warning others to be vigilant, as SA Police warn the number of incidents has increased in the state in the past year.

items.title: Dark Mofo returns with art, food and sell-out events
items.description: Tasmania's two-week Dark Mofo festival kicks off today in Hobart. Popular events such as Winter Feast, Night Mass, the Nude Solstice Swim and the Ogoh Ogoh procession return, while one of the new Spirit of Tasmania ferries will host a free art exhibition.

items.title: 'You're isolated out here': Queensland's rapidly expanding suburbs cut off
items.description: Hundreds of thousands of new homes are being built on the outskirts of greater Brisbane. But residents are concerned if one thing doesn't improve, their quality of life will go backwards.

items.title: Commonwealth Bank pursued in High Court by shareholders
items.description: The applicants want compensation for the "inflated value of their shares attributable to the bank's wrongful failure to inform the market".

items.title: Hundreds protest against Pauline Hanson as WA Labor seats on 'hit list'
items.description: A crowd of about 400 protesters demonstrates against One Nation's Pauline Hanson as she speaks at a sundowner event in Perth's eastern suburbs.

items.title: Mexico City welcomes World Cup but reality bites for many
items.description: As Mexicans prepare to host or co-host the FIFA World Cup for a record third time, many locals are frustrated by being locked out of the tournament, while others are more optimistic.

items.title: Bill Gates 'deeply sorry' for Epstein ties in testimony to US politicians
items.description: The Microsoft co-founder appeared before a closed-door US House Oversight Committee panel that has been investigating the late sex offender's connections with the rich and powerful.
